published_text: {A} finds a magnifying glass beneath the workbench. The tiny wheel markings finally stop looking identical.
{A} photographs a full-size Bone Shaker display, then returns to the table with the tiny racer that fits their lane.
{A}'s capsule visits the 1968 package artwork, then the 2008 Custom Otto display. They return with a catalogue note, leaving the models behind.
{A} tightens the new wheel until it rubs against the body. Their Hot Wheels stops halfway down the elimination track. They're out.
{A}'s registered racer rolls off the tilted workbench. A snapped front axle ends their run before the next heat.
{A}'s chipped mainline rolls past {B}'s display Hot Wheels in the deciding heat. {B} leaves with the nicer paint and no place in the race.
{A}'s Hot Wheels clears the workbench straight first. {B} reaches the finish a wheel behind and leaves the elimination bracket.
{A} announces a rare factory error. {B} removes a crumb from the wheel. The mystery is over.
{A} tests the empty lane while {B} checks the table. A folded catalogue under one leg levels the track.
The Ripper slides a {model} across the workbench to {A}. A red ribbon marks this Hot Wheels for the next heat.
{H} sends the earlier {item} down the deciding lane. {B}'s entry stalls at the loop. {B} is out, and {H} retrieves the Hot Wheels.
{H} gifts the {item} to {A}. The same Hot Wheels leaves one display and joins the other.
{A} checks the copyright date, then the release reference. The Hot Wheels is newer than the number underneath it suggests.
{A} finds a blue AMX and asks where the Ed Shaver decal sheet went. The model name is only half the question.
{A} finds a Hot Wheels without its usual graphics and checks for repainting before describing it as a factory error.
At the deciding identification desk, {A} uses the wrong year's checklist. Their submitted entry fails, ending the hunt.
{B} picks the brighter paint. {A} checks the release details and selects the correct Hot Wheels. {B} loses the deciding round.
{B} matches the casting but misses the decoration. {A} submits the requested release and takes the final place.
{A} wins the auction lot and opens the box. One display sign, no Hot Wheels. They read the lot description this time.
{A} finds their convention badge inside the display-case pocket and gets through the door without borrowing anyone else's name.
{A} examines the Candy Striper's numbered package, then returns it to the owner's display case.
{A} negotiates over one final colour variation until the race desk closes. Their empty lane costs them the heat. They're out.
A display trolley jolts into {A}'s loose race Hot Wheels. One bent axle later, {A} has no entry for the deciding heat.
{A}'s stock racer wins by its front wheels. {B} finishes the run, but their convention tournament ends there.
{A} and {B} receive fresh stock Hot Wheels at the race desk. {A} wins the deciding run. {B} leaves the bracket.
{A} takes the stairs while {B} waits with three collectors and six display cases for the elevator.
{A} and {B} move the disputed colour variation under the neutral inspection lamp. The hotel lighting stops deciding the argument.
{A} moves the Hot Wheels away from the yellow lamp before naming its colour. The argument gets quieter under daylight.
{A} turns the early Python over. The Cheetah name underneath earns the Hot Wheels a second, longer inspection.
{A} studies the resin body under the desk lamp. It belongs to the design table, away from the elimination slope.
{A} sends their registered Hot Wheels down the test slope with a bent axle. It scrapes to a halt and fails the elimination run.
{A}'s racer hits the booster off-centre, clears the table, and lands on its front axle. Their race ends there.
{A}'s Twin Mill crosses first in the deciding downhill run. {B} picks up their Hot Wheels and leaves the bracket.
{A}'s period racer stays straight through the last bend. {B}'s Hot Wheels leaves the lane, and their elimination run ends.
{A} stops at the wrong blue-and-orange pit board. The crew points one garage down before anyone touches the race car.
{A} notices a new vibration and brings the race car into the pits before attempting another full-speed lap.
{A} spots the service-road sign before turning off the circuit and stays on the marked race route.
{A}'s oil pressure falls on the straight. They stop behind the barrier, and the crew retires the race car.
Loose bodywork folds into {A}'s front tyre on the straight. They stop safely, but the damaged wheel ends their race.
{A} holds the inside line through the final corner. {B} finishes behind them and loses the elimination duel.
{A} exits the final bend ahead. {B} finishes safely behind them and loses the deciding duel.
{A} checks the edition before copying a rarity label from another release of the same famous casting.
{A} moves from the WAX archive shelf to the later Flow exhibit and keeps the two collection histories separately labelled.
{A} enlarges the Hot Wheels preview across the whole wall. The display grows, while the labelled die-cast scale stays the same.
{A} submits a screenshot to the ownership desk. The matching entry belongs to another avatar. {A} is out.
{B} selects the right model name but the wrong edition. {A} matches the full record and wins the deciding comparison.
{A}'s rendered racer clears the final bend. {B}'s Hot Wheels slides into the display barrier, ending their virtual-track run.
{A} and {B} compare matching Hot Wheels images, then notice the different edition numbers in their exhibit records.
